22914: Southwest Missouri State University, Springfield, Missouri, USA1; Chulalongkorn University, Bangkok, Thailand2 The Thai narrow-headed softshelled turtle Chitra chitra is one of the most critically endangered freshwater turtles in the world. We considered it a prime candidate for a captive breeding and head starting program due to the small number of individuals believed remaining in the wild, and a program based at the Kanchanburi Inland Fisheries Development Center in Kanchanburi, Thailand was implemented in 2000 to rehabilitate the species. The results to date are encouraging with the propagation of several hundred healthy yearlings from 700 eggs produced by six breeding adults (4 males and 2 females) in 2001 and 2002, and another 270 eggs currently incubating at the hatchery from this year’s nesting. Concurrent with the CB/HS operation, field work has been conducted to locate extant wild individuals/populations, to determine the characteristics and locations of remaining optimal habitat for potential juvenile release sites, and to identify and mitigate factors that threaten Chitra’s survival in the wild. In this presentation the CB/HS protocol and associated field studies will be described and plans for monitoring Chitra’s recovery will be discussed. The broader implications of our approach toward the conservation of other endangered freshwater turtles will also be examined.

22916: Caixa Postal 478, 69011-970 Manaus, AM Brasil In 1997-1998 an ecological study was undertaken on the use of turtles by commercial and subsistence fishermen. The results were analyzed in terms of turtle catch and conservation goals. The monitoring was made by counting and measuring shells in gardens and live animals stored in kraals. Values of niche dimensions, such as distance, gear used and season were obtained through systematic interviewing in two settlements. Of the 710 turtles and shells observed during the period 1992 to 2000, 74% were of cabeçuda Peltocephalus dumerilianus and tracajá Podocnemis unifilis. Catch levels appeared to be sustainable, and impacts on species used as bait such as jacaretinga Caiman crocodilus, and on habitats such as impact of intentional burning, were assessed and found to be minimal. The ribeirinhos participation on resource management had improved considerably and a degree of joint management had been achieved. Subsistence and commercial fishermen usually fish at different distances from settlements; they target the same species, using the same gear, but with different frequency.. Ecological concepts, such as niche and competition, may help to understand strategies of exploitation of resources, an important information for the management and conservation of Amazonian turtles. Key Words: turtles fisheries, applied ecology, cultural ecology, niche, local management, Amazon.

22917: Ghislaine Guyot Jackson, 6416 Dancer’s Image Trail, 32309 Tallahassee Florida USA, Habitat fragmentation is now the major threat facing many turtles worldwide. The re- creation of safe connections is an important conservation tool that can increase the probability of survival of local populations. Here are three examples: The western swamp turtle Pseudemydura umbrina from Western Australia is one of the rarest turtles in the world. A fence was erected around the inhabited swamp to protect the last population from exotic predators. However, a few adults of high reproductive value were trapped outside. We designed a one-way gate that allowed turtles to enter but not leave the preserve. This gate was also designed to avoid use by predators. The long-necked turtle Chelodina oblonga has a small range in southwestern Australia. In downtown Perth, city parks may host sizeable populations, often completely surrounded by housing developments. Public awareness has been raised by erecting signs in some suburbs to reduce road-kill. Two-way gates have also been installed in a Preserve to reduce mortality from predation and thermal stress along the fences. The Hermann’s tortoise Testudo hermanni occupies Mediterranean countries from Spain to eastern Turkey. The western populations are highly threatened by urbanization. Fences and tunnels tried to reconnect habitat fragments separated by a French highway.
